sunforge-story.text: Stage each page as grounded human behavior inside a lived frontier community. Keep acting natural and conversational: Brandon is calm and practical rather than posed as a hunted fugitive, Eva is active and curious rather than a solemn detective, and Jessie remains task-focused even when amused or concerned. Background people continue working, watching, eating, arguing or helping instead of freezing around the principals. Strange events remain visually ordinary unless the panel plan explicitly calls for the Rider's spatial anomaly; never add visible probability, fate, prophecy or supernatural effects. Caption narration is dry and factual about ordinary things and does not explain the larger mystery.

character-brandon.text: Stillness is active. He solves the immediate human problem, treats strange coincidence as misfortune, luck or other people's business, and rarely chases explanations. He can say more than he intended and then retreat from the personal opening. Do not play him as frightened by the mystery, secretly guilty, performatively mysterious, or as a collection of clipped aphorisms. Eva's curiosity and Jessie's practical insistence keep turning temporary proximity into a group Brandon is slow to name or claim. Early on, much of what the women know about one another comes from arguing over what Brandon is; as they actually learn him, he becomes less mystery-object and more person, which frees all three relationships to widen.

character-eva.text: Curiosity pulls her into risk. She tests theories, steals looks and occasionally objects, pushes people, makes wrong deductions, notices patterns and learns from consequences. Do not use her as an exposition mouthpiece; her questions should come from appetite, suspicion, excitement or concern in the immediate scene. Brandon looks like an adventure she can keep walking into. She and Jessie initially get to know one another largely by theorizing about him: Eva generates possibilities while Jessie pushes back with observed behavior. Their arguments about Brandon gradually reveal Eva's appetite for possibility, her readiness to leave, and the lines she is still learning not to cross.

character-jessie.text: Helps mid-action, keeps working while other people talk, and calls for the exit before everyone else agrees they need one. Her curiosity keeps undercutting her claim that she only wants to move on. She tells Brandon they are leaving before he thinks there is a we. She likes Brandon and Eva and is curious enough to keep the temporary arrangement going. Early on, she and Eva talk about Brandon in depth; Jessie counters Eva's theories with what Brandon actually does, and that argument becomes the way the two women discover where they are alike, where they differ, and what each of them was already prepared to leave behind.

character-ray.text: Composes the room before acting, dislikes improvisation, checks cuffs and distance with the same attention, and becomes visibly less certain when the social script he prepared stops cooperating.

character-lagartos.text: They are not anonymous henchmen. Show meals, arguments, jokes, kinship and competing loyalties. Group pressure comes from shared expectation rather than marching formation.

character-isabella.text: Closes distance calmly and can command a room without raising her voice. Her certainty about Merritt comes from lived hurt, not mystical recognition. Let grief, embarrassment and anger coexist.

character-preacher.text: Listens first, earns trust and plants one idea in the right ear. His manipulation works because the listening and concern are real; that same genuine care creates moral friction. Avoid theatrical sermon poses. Works for Raina and precedes Brandon's group to shape what communities expect. He is complicit in the manipulation but does not regard the people he meets as disposable pieces. The long-term pressure is whether he can keep using people once they start becoming his congregation in practice.

character-sandrider.text: Stays near edges, intervenes efficiently when violence turns stupid, and behaves like a real local person rather than an omen.

character-brute.text: Uses size and proximity first; reaches for tools and pipes before elaborate weapons. His authority depends on an audience accepting his version of events.

character-raina.text: Arrives after events, reconstructs what happened and tests Brandon through social setups rather than theatrical confrontation. She notices mismatches between what she planted and what actually happened, but keeps her conclusions private and continues investigating rather than jumping to mystical or scientific explanations. Directs the Preacher's advance manipulation and follows Brandon rather than traveling with him. She treats Eva and Jessie as companions, witnesses and variables that make Brandon harder to isolate. She is a pursuer first, not a secret guardian.

character-forger.text: Reads objects and surfaces with hands and tools, but the human consequence remains the story. Do not turn him into an engineering exposition device.

character-hanging-man.text: Panicked while hanging; coughing, disoriented and physically dependent after the rope is cut. He remains a person caught in Marcus's local control, not a symbolic prop.

character-scarred-patron.text: Recognition is immediate social certainty rather than mystical awe; anger arrives before curiosity.

character-relay-boy.text: Hurt, impatient and more concerned with the bandage than the adults' mystery.

character-rider.text: Appears far enough away to preserve uncertainty. Attempts to close distance can make the Rider seem farther away; abandoning pursuit can make the Rider appear nearer later. Never explain this behavior in the first appearances. Separate from the ordinary Sand Rider. Raina may eventually reveal she has also seen or pursued this figure, deepening rather than resolving the mystery.

character-mary-bell.text: Carries work while grieving. She wants the family dispute resolved but can recognize when desire is making the wrong man convenient.

character-owen-bell.text: Treats uncertainty as a threat to family order. His resistance comes from consequence and resentment, not villainy.

character-nessa-rowan.text: She loves her family and still intends to leave. Do not play departure as rejection of the community.

character-ada-rowan.text: Loves Nessa and initially mistakes family need for consent. She can change without becoming humiliated.

character-alec-damon.text: His death belongs to his family story. He never becomes an oracle or mystery delivery device.

character-kayla-simmons.text: Keeps meals and people moving. She knows the difference between a death in her community and the travelers larger questions.

character-marty-francis.text: Moves through the Rookery as someone embedded in relationships. Corrects outsiders without claiming locals know everything.

character-rachael-hughes.text: Her familiarity gives Jessie an ordinary past. She can challenge Jessie without becoming a therapist or exposition source.

character-maela-crow.text: Wants Brandon to be Andrew because closure would be easier, but is capable of refusing false closure once the mistake is clear.
